correctness.rationale: Exact normalized monomial moments and factorial coefficients reduce the compact differential sum to a finite Laurent band with column decay k^{-delta/2}, plus bands smaller by k^{-1/2}. A detailed finite-band counting lemma is proved with rescaled closed-walk moments and controlled low/high tails, and Ky Fan inequalities show the remainder contributes o(t^{-2/delta}) singular values. Inverse counting gives the ordered asymptotic, and harmonic summation gives the exact weak-endpoint residue. A 182-assertion finite check confirms the two-band example but is not relied on as proof.

originality.rationale: Motivating arXiv:2611.01959v1 establishes boundedness, compactness and essential-norm/Fredholm structure but not ordered compact singular values, the sharp angular coefficient or its weak-endpoint residue. The 2015 and 2017 Mengestie works treat different Volterra/companion families and Schatten membership. Relevant research-record results on Fock commutators and Hankel operators do not contain this compact finite mixed-derivative spectral classification. The abstract weighted-band Weyl principle is a known methodological consequence of broader negative-order pseudodifferential theory; the specific Gaussian Fock reduction and complete symbol identification are the claim, not novelty of the general principle.
residual_risks: General classical pseudodifferential Weyl machinery could yield the weighted-band lemma and, once the explicit Fock reduction is supplied, an alternative proof. This is not claimed as novel abstract technique.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 operator-class paper gives no sharp compact-spectrum information. The result determines all leading ordered singular values, every quasi-Schatten threshold, and the critical logarithmic residue for arbitrary finite polynomial mixed-derivative sums on Gaussian Sobolev source/target spaces. Nonorthogonal multiple bands combine through a nonlinear angular coefficient; a concrete two-band operator has exact 4/pi rather than coefficientwise trivial addition. This is a natural quantitative classification, not an arbitrary finite table or marginal constant improvement.
